mcq.q: Which type of entrepreneur copies existing products made by innovators and imitates their technology, process and methods?
mcq.e: The imitating entrepreneur copies the innovative entrepreneur's products, technology, process and methods.

mcq.q: Which entrepreneur is skeptical about change and waits for the outcome of released products in the market before starting the next project?
mcq.e: The Fabian entrepreneur is skeptical about change and waits to see how released products fare.

mcq.q: Which entrepreneur is happy with business results even with financial losses and is reluctant to make any change?
mcq.e: The drone entrepreneur is reluctant to change and content with results even when they involve financial losses.

mcq.q: Which entrepreneur has a great passion for discovering new products, ideas and processes and enjoys the challenge of risk?
mcq.e: The innovative entrepreneur is passionate about discovering new products, ideas and processes and enjoys risk.

mcq.q: Entrepreneurship is described as "creating the new and destroying the old." Which of these is NOT listed as something new?
mcq.e: The slide lists new knowledge, products, processes, services, markets, business models and raw materials; taxes are not on it.

mcq.q: According to Kuratko and Hodgetts (2007), an entrepreneur is an innovator who recognizes opportunities, adds value, and also:
mcq.a: Assumes the risks of the competitive marketplace and realizes the rewards
mcq.e: Kuratko and Hodgetts describe the entrepreneur as one who assumes the risks of the competitive marketplace and realizes the rewards.

mcq.q: A technopreneur is defined by Daniel Mankani (2003) as an entrepreneur who:
mcq.a: Uses cutting-edge technology to develop a new business
mcq.e: Mankani (2003) defines a technopreneur as an entrepreneur who uses cutting-edge technology to develop a new business.

mcq.q: Technopreneurship is best described as:
mcq.e: Technopreneurship is entrepreneurship in a technology-intensive context, merging technology prowess with entrepreneurial skills.

mcq.q: Technology Developers, who create unique technology capable of driving a new business, are also known as:
mcq.e: Technology developers, who create the technology, are the inventors.

mcq.q: Technology Users, who see a new technology and apply it to meet a new market need, are also known as:
mcq.e: Technology users, who spot how a new technology meets a market need, are the innovators.

mcq.q: Which is NOT considered a technology-based enterprise even though it uses computers?
mcq.e: An internet café uses computers in operations but is not a technology-based enterprise.

mcq.q: The slide cites which Apple innovation as a technopreneurship example with a 160 GB, 1.8-inch hard disk drive?
mcq.e: The iPod example is the 160 GB, 1.8-inch hard disk drive.

mcq.q: Which company is cited for offering one-day delivery anywhere in the world through its sorting and delivery facility?
mcq.e: UPS is the slide's example of one-day delivery anywhere in the world.

mcq.q: How many stages are in the technopreneurial process shown in the slides?
mcq.e: The technopreneurial process has 8 steps, from idea generation to monitoring and evaluation.

mcq.q: Which is the FIRST step of the technopreneurial process?
mcq.e: Idea generation is step 1 of the technopreneurial process.

mcq.q: Which is the LAST step of the technopreneurial process?
mcq.e: Monitoring and evaluation is step 8, after commercialization.

mcq.q: In the technopreneurial process, which step comes right after concept testing?
mcq.e: Business analysis is step 4, right after concept testing.

mcq.q: The 5 steps of the entrepreneurial process end with:
mcq.e: The entrepreneurial process ends with scaling and harvesting (step 5).

mcq.q: Innovation that happens incrementally, as a response to customer and market demands, is called:
mcq.e: Sustaining innovation is incremental and responds to customer and market demands.

mcq.q: Another name for sustaining innovation is:
mcq.e: Sustaining innovation is also called routine innovation.

mcq.q: Which companies are cited as examples of sustaining innovation?
mcq.e: The slides cite Apple, Intel and Amazon as sustaining innovators.

mcq.q: Who popularized the idea of disruptive innovation?
mcq.e: Clayton Christensen popularized disruptive innovation.

mcq.q: Which Clayton Christensen book was published in 1997?
mcq.e: Christensen's The Innovator's Dilemma was published in 1997.

mcq.q: A classic example of disruptive innovation given in the slides is:
mcq.e: Cellphones displacing fixed-line telephony is the slides' classic disruptive example.

mcq.q: Innovation that comes from inside a company and pushes something to the next level, opening new markets, is called:
mcq.e: Breakthrough innovation comes from inside a company, pushes something to the next level and opens new markets.

mcq.q: Which product is the slide's example of breakthrough innovation?
mcq.e: The slides use the Apple iPhone as the breakthrough example.

mcq.q: Innovation that begins with the discovery of a new phenomenon and seeks to understand how nature and people are put together is:
mcq.e: Basic research starts with discovering a new phenomenon to learn how nature and people are put together.

mcq.q: Which principle of sustainable innovation states that new products must solve real customer problems?
mcq.e: Value creation means new products must solve real customer problems.

mcq.q: Which principle says that team members and leaders have full responsibility and obligation in the innovation?
mcq.e: Accountability means the team and leaders carry full responsibility for the innovation.

mcq.q: Which principle says that achieving the ROI should be followed by incentives for employees?
mcq.e: Net result and reward: when the ROI is achieved, employees get incentives.

mcq.q: "Technopreneurs are risk takers" matches which principle for sustainable innovation?
mcq.e: "No risk, no innovation" is the principle that technopreneurs are risk takers.

mcq.q: In idea selection, the "ABC analysis" is used in which step?
mcq.e: Rough selection, the first of three idea-selection steps, uses ABC analysis.

mcq.q: In the ABC analysis, which ideas are discussed and decided on together?
mcq.e: B-ideas are uncertain, so they are discussed and decided together.

mcq.q: In the ABC analysis, C-ideas are:
mcq.e: C-ideas have no value and are rejected.

mcq.q: In the "dots gluing" method of fine selection, how many sticky points does each participant receive?
mcq.e: In dot gluing each participant gets 5 sticky points to distribute among ideas.

mcq.q: When there are fewer than ten ideas, fine selection can use the "rating" method with points from:
mcq.e: With fewer than ten ideas, each participant rates every idea from 0 to 5 points.

mcq.q: Which is a criterion used in the detailed analysis of product ideas?
mcq.e: Detailed analysis judges customer benefit, differentiation and competitive factor, and technical and economic feasibility.

mcq.q: A canvas by which person can be used in detailed analysis for new business models?
mcq.e: Osterwalder's canvas can be used in detailed analysis for new business models.

mcq.q: A focus group typically consists of how many people with a moderator?
mcq.e: A focus group is typically 8 to 12 people led by a moderator.

mcq.q: The researcher gathers information by simply watching how a subject interacts with a product. This technique is:
mcq.e: Observation means watching how a subject interacts with a product.

mcq.q: A one-on-one interview using probing questions to understand a person's product preferences is a(n):
mcq.e: An in-depth interview is one-on-one with probing questions.

mcq.q: Determining whether your product is of interest to a target market, usually before significant investment, is called:
mcq.e: Market validation checks whether a target market is interested in your product, usually before significant investment.

mcq.q: What is the FIRST of the 5 steps to determine market validation?
mcq.a: Write down goals, assumptions and hypotheses
mcq.e: Step 1 of market validation is writing down goals, assumptions and hypotheses.

mcq.q: Which is the LAST of the 5 steps of market validation?
w: Research search volume of related terms
mcq.e: Step 5, the last step, is testing the product or service with alpha and beta testing.

mcq.q: Testing by internal employees in a staged setting to eliminate bugs before outside users see the product is:
mcq.e: Alpha testing uses internal employees in a staged setting to remove bugs before outsiders see the product.

mcq.q: Testing by a limited group of real external users who are told to identify problems is:
mcq.e: Beta testing uses a limited group of real external users told to find problems.

mcq.q: Which stage of the decision-making process comes right after "Information search"?
mcq.e: Information search is followed by evaluation of alternatives.

mcq.q: The 5th and last stage of the decision-making process is:
mcq.e: The five stages end with evaluation of the decision.

mcq.q: The Business Model Canvas was proposed by:
mcq.e: Alexander Osterwalder proposed the Business Model Canvas (the slides also follow Alex Cowan's explanation).

mcq.q: How many building blocks does the Business Model Canvas have?
mcq.e: The Business Model Canvas has 9 building blocks.

mcq.q: Which BMC block answers "Who are the customers? What do they think, see, feel, do?"
mcq.e: Customer segments asks who the customers are and what they think, see, feel and do.

mcq.q: A media property such as CNN.com with readers on one side and advertisers on the other is an example of a:
mcq.e: CNN.com serves readers and advertisers, which makes it a multi-sided market.

mcq.q: Which BMC block is "the value a company promises to deliver to customers should they choose to buy"?
mcq.e: The value proposition is the value the company promises to deliver to customers.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the five phases of channels?
mcq.e: The five channel phases are awareness, evaluation, purchase, delivery and after sales; production is not one.

mcq.q: In the channel phases, "word of mouth, social media, newspaper, television and flyers" belong to which phase?
mcq.e: Word of mouth, social media, newspapers, TV and flyers are awareness channels.

mcq.q: Which are the 3 benefits of good customer relationships listed in the slides?
mcq.e: Good customer relationships bring retention, loyalty and satisfaction.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a way to generate revenue streams listed in the slides?
mcq.e: Crowdfunding is a way to raise startup capital, not one of the slide's revenue-stream types.

mcq.q: Which BMC block asks "What can the company not do so it can focus on its key activities?"
mcq.e: The slide's key partnerships block is described as what the company will not do itself, so it can focus on key activities.

mcq.q: A strategic alliance between competitors is called:
mcq.e: Coopetition is cooperation between competitors, as listed under key partnerships.

mcq.q: According to the slides, what percent of Google's revenue comes from advertising?
mcq.e: The slide says 97% of Google's revenue comes from advertising.

mcq.q: A cost structure focused on creating more value in the product rather than the lowest cost is:
mcq.e: Value-driven cost structures focus on creating more value in the product rather than the lowest cost.

mcq.q: A cost structure focused on minimizing costs of the product or service is:
mcq.e: Cost-driven cost structures focus on minimizing the cost of the product or service.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a type of key resource listed in the slides?
mcq.e: The key resource types are physical, intellectual, human and financial; political is not one.

mcq.q: Patents, brands, copyrights and customer lists are what kind of key resources?
mcq.e: Patents, brands, copyrights and customer lists are intellectual resources.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the five types of intellectual property rights?
mcq.e: The five IP types are copyright, patents, trade secrets, trademarks and industrial design; a franchise is a business arrangement.

mcq.q: Which IP right protects literary and artistic works, including computer programs and databases?
mcq.e: Copyright protects literary and artistic works, including computer programs and databases.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a right granted under copyright law?
mcq.e: Copyright rights cover reproducing, derivative works, distributing, and public performance and display; patenting is a different right.

mcq.q: Patent applications in the Philippines are published in the:
mcq.e: Philippine patent applications are published in the IPO Gazette, where anyone may contest them.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a type of patent mentioned in the slides?
mcq.e: The slide patent types are utility, design and plant; a process falls under utility.

mcq.q: A patent covering an original, new and ornamental design for a manufactured product is a:
mcq.e: A design patent covers an original, new and ornamental design.

mcq.q: A practice or process generally unknown outside the company that gives an economic advantage is a:
mcq.e: A trade secret is a practice or process not generally known outside the company that gives it an economic advantage.

mcq.q: A special trademark that designates protection for services is a:
mcq.e: A service mark protects services, as distinct from products.

mcq.q: A special trademark owned by an organization or association is a:
mcq.e: A collective mark is owned by an organization or association.

mcq.q: A mark registered to ascertain adherence to local regulations is a:
mcq.e: A certification mark is registered to ascertain adherence to local regulations.

mcq.q: The ornamental or aesthetic aspect of an article, including 3D shape or 2D patterns, is covered by:
mcq.e: Industrial design protects the ornamental or aesthetic aspect of an article, in 3D shape or 2D patterns.

mcq.q: Which investors make high-risk investments in early-stage ventures as individuals?
mcq.e: Angel investors are individuals making high-risk investments in early-stage ventures.

mcq.q: Which investors invest in relatively mature ventures with a track record in a 1–5 year time frame?
mcq.e: Private equity firms invest in relatively mature ventures with a track record, on a 1–5 year time frame.

mcq.q: Which source of funds offers the lowest cost of capital according to the slides?
mcq.e: The slides say banks offer the lowest cost of capital.

mcq.q: Strategic investors are usually:
mcq.a: Larger companies in the same industry
mcq.e: Strategic investors are usually larger companies in the same industry.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a way of raising capital for startups listed in the slides?
mcq.e: The slide's capital-raising ways are self-funding, crowdfunding, friends and family, loans and competitions.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a component of a small business financial plan?
mcq.e: Small-business financial plan components are statements, projections, ratios and break-even analysis; a marketing slogan is not one.

mcq.q: Determining capital requirements and capital structure are objectives of:
mcq.e: Financial planning determines capital requirements and capital structure, among other objectives.

mcq.q: A document that summarizes operational and financial objectives with detailed plans and budgets is a:
mcq.e: A business plan summarizes operational and financial objectives with detailed plans and budgets.

mcq.q: How many sections are in the business plan outline in the slides?
mcq.e: The business plan outline has 7 sections.

mcq.q: Which section of the business plan comes FIRST?
mcq.e: The executive summary comes first in the outline.

mcq.q: Which section is the LAST in the business plan outline?
mcq.e: The financial plan is the 7th and last section.

mcq.q: How many blocks does the Lean Canvas have?
mcq.e: The Lean Canvas has 9 blocks.

mcq.q: Which is a block of the Lean Canvas in the slides?
mcq.e: Unfair advantage is a Lean Canvas block; key partnerships, customer relationships and key resources belong to the Business Model Canvas.

mcq.q: An elevator pitch is usually how long?
mcq.e: An elevator pitch is concise, usually 30 seconds to 2 minutes.

mcq.q: What is the FIRST step of the 5-step elevator pitch?
mcq.e: Step 1 of the pitch is introducing yourself with your name, company and service.

mcq.q: What is the LAST step of the 5-step elevator pitch?
mcq.a: Know when to stop and listen
mcq.e: Step 5 is knowing when to stop and listen.

mcq.q: Which of the three essential components of a pitch is the most important?
mcq.e: Stimulating interest is the most important of the three pitch components.

mcq.q: The "100/20 Rule" is associated with which pitch component?
mcq.e: The 100/20 Rule backs the "share a vision" component, the value proposition.
